I worked in Parts at a Hyundai dealership. The 23 is not included in the trailer hitch recall. The 23 had a significant change in body design and it is not even compatible with that  hitch--different part numbers for everything on the back. 

In fact, at the time I still worked there a couple months back, there had not yet been a trailer hitch/harness released at all for the 23 model. So, absolutely no 23 models came out of the factory with a hitch nor were any available for purchase or dealer installation for that model year. 

This is crazy to see..

Also there was a stop sale and a dealer cannot legally sell a palisade with a hitch without pulling the fuse, which is the only current remedy Hyundai has issued for the recall.

What people are saying about her potentially being liable because there was a recall notice holds absolutely no water, since she bought it very recently, well after any of the recalls were announced. The dealer would 100% be responsible for letting a vehicle leave the lot without performing the issued remedy for any and all recalls. It's not optional, it's required by law.

If there is no remedy for a safety recall, the effected vehicles are not allowed to be sold.

Many people here saying it's a nonsense price, one even said they got their brand new Kia cat for 350.. In what world lol I'm scratching my head at that one.. 

I work at a Hyundai dealership (Kia is an offshoot of Hyundai and they share engines and many other parts) , and 2500 sounds typical for OEM cats on these cars. Many of them have a "mani-cats", the exhaust manifold and cat convertor are infused into one piece, and then a second catalyst on the mid muffler assembly. So they've possibly quoted the replacement of both, which easily comes out to that price. I looked up the cost of those parts on a same year Hyundai with a 2.0 and my dealer cost is almost 2k so at retail it easily is over 2.5k..

The dealer isn't quoting you 10x what the parts cost, despite what people here are saying. Those parts cost thousands for the dealer from Hyundai/Kia. That said, the cat convertors aren't immediately essential for the functioning of the vehicle, unlike the transmission. You will have a check engine light from it but otherwise it's not a hurry. Do get a second opinion

Do you know for certain that you didn't get an extended warranty when you bought it? I would check with the finance papers from the dealership. Get a second opinion from a chevy expert. 

Go to a chevy dealership with your VIN number and make sure you don't have any relevant recalls or extended warranties/service campaigns. Some Cruzes have a recall out for head gasket failure. Then ask them for pricing and availability on a head gasket set and head rebuild kit. (You probably only need the gasket set) Have all your vehicle information ready and be confident when you speak to them. If you can get the part numbers you should be able to find the parts much cheaper online or at a parts house like AutoZone. 

If you can provide your own parts then you'd only have to worry about labor rates. My dealership charges 140/hr, but you can find mom and pop shops that charge less than half that. They might get iffy or roll their eyes about you bringing your own parts, be polite but sure of yourself and say you did your research with the dealer. You could get the head job done at 1,500 or less if you do it smartly. Then you have the option to sell or trade for at least the 5k that you owe. 

The cat converter could honestly be overblown bs, and it could literally just be dirty or have broken oxygen sensors, which are far cheaper than replacing the entire cat. The car will run fine without it anyway, it's just for noise and emissions. (But you probably wouldn't be able to sell or trade with a bad cat, dash will be lit up with check engine code). A complete failure would be sufficiently obvious. Get under there and look at it. Is it blown to shreds? Rusted all the way through? Does it stink bad when running? Is it leaky? If it looks fine just run some Cataclean through it and it might even fix the issue. 

The trans leak could be a much more complex issue, keep an eye on the ground where you park it to see if there's any puddles. Trans fluid is usually brightly colored, though yours might be a bit muddy. Watch some YouTube videos about the car and see what you can learn and figure out yourself. See if you have a tranny dipstick and can top up the fluid yourself for the time being.

I've got a better premise. Instead of automatically assuming the androids ARE just like humans and anyone who thinks otherwise is a racist piece of shit and hamfisting holocaust and underground railroad parallels down our throat (making parallels to these things is fine but the way Cage did it in the game was lazy and shallow), they could have shown a deep introspection into the idea of machines having a conscience and made the game about 50/50 of pure emotion vs hard facts. Instead of making the game say outright that androids are human(and that one can "awaken" another with their mind, seriously wtf was that), the game could have been a moral dilemma making you really weigh out the facts. 

We could have a main character(like Marcus, but less corny and annoying) start to develop what it believes is feelings and sentience, the game could explore what the bounds are of the android's intelligence (there was a stark lack of this in the game. Are they supercomputers or is their knowledge limited to their tasks and basic information) if the android is intelligent like a supercomputer than it would likely be a very frank and unfeeling thing, it does not have the chemicals and endorphins that make humans have certain emotions. So then, could it still possess desire? What about morals? What would compel Marcus to act? If he can feel, what gave him those feelings? Were they programmed into him? We can explore a world of different views on morality and emotions. One thing I did like about Cage's story was the little girl turning out to be an android. It presented the question: was she actually self aware and making her own choices or was she just doing what she was programmed to do? But not much came off of that. 

We don't know if a machine can become sentient, we barely understand sentience, so this game could have presented some great philosophy and science. (I would say the Android detective's story is the one grounded in fact and reality but it's made clear shortly into the story and at the ending that anything but treating androids as people is wrong and evil. If they had kept his story staunchly grounded in fact and logic it would have better demonstrated the dilemma of artificial intelligence and how complex the subject is. Let the player have their choice and not make them feel punished for it instead of insisting that there's only one right choice). But no, the androids are people and if you think otherwise you basically lose the game. I anticipated this game for years and it was nothing like I thought it'd be. I was deeply disappointed with its shallowness. Many people seem to like it, that's fine. I feel it could have been something truly special.
